[← Telecom](../index.qmd)

An advanced course on the 5G NR air interface for radio planning,
optimization and RF design engineers. Every topic goes from the 3GPP
definition to the equation behind it and then to the field: what to
configure, what to measure, and how to recognise the problem in a drive test
or a counter.

**Prerequisite:** working knowledge of LTE or NR basics, OFDM, decibels and
link budgets. The course accompanies the *5G Under the Hood* LinkedIn series
and goes several levels deeper. Each deck cites the exact 3GPP clauses, so
every number can be checked against the Release you work with.

## How to study with these slides

1. Read the deck once for the structure. Press **S** for speaker notes: they
   hold the derivations, field context and the exercise answers.
2. Redo every worked example yourself, then change one input (band, SCS,
   distance) and predict the result before computing it.
3. Open the cited 3GPP clause next to the slide. The goal is to read the
   specification directly, with this course as the map.
4. Take one live cell's configuration (RACH-ConfigCommon, TDD pattern, SSB
   settings) and re-derive its range, overhead and measurement behaviour with
   the formulas from the course.

## Sources

- 3GPP TS 38.101-1, 38.104, 38.133, 38.211, 38.212, 38.213, 38.214, 38.215,
  38.300, 38.304, 38.321, 38.331 and TR 38.901, Rel-15 to Rel-17, free from
  [3gpp.org](https://www.3gpp.org/specifications-technologies).
- [ShareTechnote](https://www.sharetechnote.com/) 5G pages: practical
  explanations, RRC examples and log traces, linked per topic in each deck.
- C. Johnson, *5G New Radio in Bullets*, independently published, 2019
  (ISBN 978-1077484351): recommended companion for the same topics.
- E. Dahlman, S. Parkvall, J. Sköld, *5G NR: The Next Generation Wireless
  Access Technology*, 2nd ed., Academic Press, 2020.
